claim: In NASA White Sands quiescent upward-burn tests following the NASA-STD-6001 Test 1 procedure, silicone rubber about 1.5 mm thick consistently self-extinguished only up to 21% oxygen at 101.3 kPa, 23% at 85.3 kPa and 28% at 48.2 kPa.
material: Silicone rubber (polysiloxane), about 1.5 mm thick, 6.4 cm wide x at least 15.2 cm long samples

conditions.pressure_text: 101.3 kPa (14.7 psia); 85.3 kPa (12.4 psia); 48.2 kPa (7 psia)
conditions.gravity: 1 g, upward burning, quiescent chamber (ground test)

limits: Ground test (1 g, upward flame spread, no forced flow), one thickness (about 1.5 mm), three pressures only; no value at 70.3 kPa or at 30% O2. MOC is the highest O2 at which samples consistently self-extinguish; it is not a microgravity or lunar-gravity result.
usefulness: (a) The gasket case. At the ISS nominal 21% O2 / 101.3 kPa silicone sits exactly at its limit (MOC 21%), and the ISS worst case of 24.1% O2 is above that 21% (derived comparison). At the lunar scenario of 30% O2 the highest tabulated silicone MOC (28% at 48.2 kPa) is still below 30%, and no pressure tested gives an MOC at or above 30%, so there is no evidence in this paper that 1.5 mm silicone self-extinguishes at 30% O2 (no test at 70.3 kPa).

The deck does not define M22759; JSC 29353B (PDF p. 22) lists "Teflon (SAE-AS-22759 (formerly MIL-W-22759) ...)" as a general-purpose wire, but equating the deck's M22759 with that specification is an inference. The deck's "1993-2004 round robin history" bullet (34% probability a sample passes, 10% all pass, 33% all fail, 52% mixed) does not restate the oxygen level or pressure and must not be shown as a 30% O2 / 10.2 psia result. JSC 29353B (PDF p. 22) says most aerospace-grade electrical wire insulation is nonflammable in ISS and human exploration environments, so this round robin must not be generalised to all wire. Ground laboratory test only.

The probabilities (34% a sample passes, 10% all pass, 33% all fail, 52% mixed) sit under the bullet "1993-2004 round robin history" on the slide "Test 4 Data Analysis on M22759 (continued)" (PDF p. 14), not under the 2006 round robin, and that bullet does not restate the oxygen level or pressure. limits: The sentence gives 30 percent oxygen with no pressure and says nothing about concentrations above 30 percent; it is a guideline statement, not a test table. The footnote printed at the bottom of the same page ("These usage limits have been demonstrated acceptable in atmospheres up to 30 percent oxygen but have not yet been tested for the higher oxygen concentrations expected for EVA-intensive...") belongs to the hook-and-loop fastener limits, not to bags, and must not be cited for bags.
